- **ReFrame Initiative**
  - Founded by the Sundance Institute and Women in Film Los Angeles (WIF).  
  - Launched the ReFrame Stamp in **2018**.  
  - Since launch, **over 800** ReFrame Stamps have been awarded.  
  - The Stamp is awarded for “gender‑balanced hiring” in scripted film and television projects.

- **2021‑2022 ReFrame TV Stamp Recipients** (200 most popular scripted series)
  - *Abbott Elementary* (ABC, Season 1)  
  - *Bridgerton* (Netflix, Season 2)  
  - *Euphoria* (HBO Max, Season 2)  
  - *Severance* (Apple TV+, Season 1)  
  - *The Great British Baking Show* – *no entry (illustrative only)*
  - *(List continues with all titles shown in the article; see Coverage section for full enumeration.)*

- **Stamp Eligibility Criteria (TV)**
  - Must hire women or individuals of other under‑represented gender identities/expressions in at least **four of eight key roles** (writer, director, producer, lead, co‑lead, and department heads).  
  - Additional points awarded for hiring women of color in key positions and for overall gender parity in the crew.

- **2021‑2022 Data Highlights**
  - **47 %** of the 200 most popular scripted series earned the ReFrame Stamp.  
  - **59** shows had a woman showrunner (29.5 % of shows); **7** of those had a woman of color showrunner (3.5 %).  
  - In episode analysis: 36 % of episodes were directed by women; 16.2 % of writers were women of color.  
  - 62.5 % of laugh‑track / comedic series nominees earned the Stamp; 40 % of major studios’ content earned the Stamp.

- **Additional Context**
  - ReFrame actively collaborates with IMDbPro to determine eligibility.  
  - The Stamp appears in the end credits of productions and has a dedicated channel on Delta Airlines.  
  - ReFrame’s expanded collaboration through 2025 will continue to use IMDbPro data.

- The ReFrame Stamp is a *gender‑balanced production certification* awarded by the *ReFrame* project to film and television productions that demonstrate proportional representation of women in key creative and production roles.  
- The program began on *June 8 2018* and is based in the *United States*.  
- The official website is *https://www.reframeproject.org/stamp*.  
- The criteria for receiving the stamp involve a points‑system awarded for female representation among directors, writers, producers, department heads and screen time; a minimum of four points, with at least two points in the categories of *female director*, *female writer*, and *female lead* is required.  
- The Stamp is awarded both to *theatrically released or streaming feature films* and to *television shows* (both broadcast and streaming).  
- Recipient lists are organized by year. For each year a set of films and TV programs that have received the stamp is listed in a table under the sections titled “2017 Narrative and Animated Feature Recipients”, “2018 Feature Recipients”, “2019 Top 100‑Grossing Narrative Feature Recipients”, “2020 Top 100‑Grossing Narrative Feature Recipients”, etc.  
- Example 2018 recipients include: *A Simple Favor*, *Acrimony*, *The Spy Who Dumped Me*, *Shannon’s* and numerous others (41 films listed).  
- Example 2019 recipients include: *A Dog’s Way Home*, *Black and Blue*, *Escape Room*, *Little Women*, *Abominable*, *Cats*, *Last Christmas*, *Little*, *Ma*, *Queen & Slim*, *Us*, etc.  
- The page contains a detailed list of winners up to the 2020–21 Top 200 Television Recipients section (covering releases through 2021).
